layer1_identification.workType: a round country boule (campagne) loaf with one quarter-wedge sliced away, revealing a spiral strawberry-jam swirl baked through the crumb
layer1_identification.broadClassification: food prop / stylized low-poly clay 3D render, game asset
layer1_identification.note: reference images are themselves AI-rendered low-poly faceted stylized renders, not photographs; runtime target is smooth matte clay per 2026-08-30 finish contract, so facet edges in the reference are a style cue, not a geometry target

layer2_form_silhouette.boundingVolume: round dome (hemisphere-like, flatter than a full sphere) with one 90-degree wedge removed down to the base, exposing a flat radial cut face
layer2_form_silhouette.symmetry: base form is radially symmetric (round boule) but broken twice: a 4-fold cross slash across the crown, and a single missing wedge sector between two of the slash arms (net symmetry: none, single dominant viewing side)
layer2_form_silhouette.shapeLanguage: smooth geometric dome base with hand-crafted surface treatment (dense banneton rings, torn slash ears) plus one deliberate flat cut

measurements_px_frontElevation.heightOverWidth: ~0.38 -- matches base campagne.ts DOME_HEIGHT=0.76 on a unit radius

derivedRatios.wedgeSpan: the missing wedge reads as one quarter of the circle (~90 degrees) in the top-down view
derivedRatios.cutFaceHeightFraction: cut face spans the full dome height, flat and vertical, from base to the crown's slash line

macro: wedge cutaway (negative space + two new flat cut faces)
meso: crust crown: dense concentric banneton-ring banding covering the entire visible dome, alternating warm mid-brown and lighter dusted bands
cross slash: 4 raised, sharply pointed ridges ('ears') meeting at the apex, reading almost as a 4-point starburst rather than a soft cross
cut faces: two new flat radial faces where the wedge was removed
micro: jam spiral: a tight red-pink Archimedean-like spiral running through the pale crumb on both exposed cut faces, roughly 3.5-4 visible turns, fairly regular width (less ragged than a hand-rolled cinnamon-bun swirl)
crumb: pale cream-white background around the spiral, small open crumb texture implied but not sharply detailed
crust edge at the cut: a thin, slightly darker crust rim where the crust meets the exposed crumb

layer4_spatial: <cross slash, centered-on, dome crown> contact: the 4 ears all meet at a single apex point at the top of the dome
<wedge cutaway, between, two slash ears> contact: the missing wedge sits squarely between two adjacent slash arms in the top-down view, not overlapping either arm

<jam spiral, embedded-in, crumb> contact: the spiral is a baked-in cross-section pattern, not a topical smear -- it appears identically on both exposed cut faces (a real physical roll would look near-mirrored/continuous across the two faces, but here it can be treated as two independent instances of the same spiral pattern for a stylized game asset)
<crust rim, wrapping, cut face edge> contact: the crust forms a thin continuous rim around each cut face's outer arc, same as the intact dome's outer crust

crust.relief: dense, closely-packed concentric ring texture (far denser than the base campagne's 8 grooves -- reads as 15-20+ bands), each ring a shallow ridge/valley pair

crumb.relief: flat cut plane, faint open-crumb suggestion, no visible pores at this resolution

jamSwirl.roughness: slightly lower than crumb -- reads a touch richer/more saturated than a flat matte paint, but no distinct specular highlight is visible at this render scale
jamSwirl.relief: the reference shows the jam as flush with the crumb face (no visible groove) -- but the prompt JSON negative list explicitly bans 'glossy jam sheen', so the intended read is a baked-in color band, not a wet pool; the img2threejs v1 build's decision to physically channel/recess the jam band (not just paint it) is what separated it from a 'stickered on' look and is retained here for that reason

layer6_color.source: assets/prompts/breads/campagne--strawberry-jam.json geometry (authoritative, hand-transcribed, JSON overrides image on any conflict)
layer6_color.crustAlbedo: #A9713F blended to a darker brown toward the base (JSON: 'amber to dark brown surface #A9713F to a darker brown blend across the dome')
layer6_color.crumbAlbedo: pale cream, no hex in JSON -- reuse campagne.ts/baguette.json CRUMB #F4EAD4 (documented series-shared constant)
layer6_color.jamAlbedo: #B23A4E (JSON: 'a deep red strawberry jam swirl #B23A4E spirals through the pale open crumb')
layer6_color.finish: crust matte; crumb matte; jam slightly richer but not glossy per the negative prompt list
layer6_color.observedVsSpec: reference crust reads warmer/more saturated on the sunlit crown facets than a flat #A9713F fill, and cooler/darker toward the base and inside the slash trenches -- consistent with the base campagne.ts tone-banding (dark/mid/light quantized by ridge phase + t) rather than a smooth gradient; jam color in the reference cut face is close to the JSON hex, slightly darkened at the spiral's inner core

layer7_identity_features: very dense banneton ring banding across the entire dome -- the single biggest visual difference from the base campagne.ts's 8-groove pattern
cross slash reads as 4 sharp pointed ears/blades meeting at one apex, closer to a pinwheel/star silhouette than a soft cross
exactly one quarter-wedge missing, sitting between two slash arms, exposing two new flat radial cut faces
jam spiral: 3.5-4 fairly regular turns, present identically on both cut faces, centered roughly in the middle of each cut face and reaching close to (but not touching) the outer crust rim

no visible loose flour dust specks in this v4 render -- the light bands read as part of the continuous ring pattern itself, not scattered dust (differs from the JSON's 'light flour dusting scattered unevenly' wording; JSON still governs color/feature presence per project convention, so a light sparse dusting is kept but de-emphasized relative to the ring banding, which is the dominant crust texture)
layer8_uncertainty: far hemisphere of the dome (opposite the wedge) is not directly shown from behind, but by radial symmetry of the base form it is treated as a smooth continuation of the same ring-banded crust -- no new geometry class inferred there

exact jam spiral turn count/thickness is not pixel-identical between the two cut faces in the reference (foreshortening in the 3/4 view) -- top-down view (-3.png) is treated as the fixed measurement plane per CRIB's 'fix the measurement plane' lesson
crumb pore/texture detail is not resolvable at the reference's render scale -- treated as a stylization choice (understated pores), not a missing feature
